Chapter 8: The Power of Service — Love in Action.
There comes a moment, often quietly, when all that searching and reflection inside you wants to find its place in the world. That love you’ve been discovering? It naturally starts to reach outward—almost like it can’t help but express itself through action.
Think about it: you’re going about your day, and you notice a neighbor struggling with heavy bags. Maybe before, you’d have hurried past, not wanting to get involved. But now, something’s different. You feel this little nudge—a sense of connection. You offer to help, and in that simple moment, both of you are changed. Sure, your neighbor is grateful, but you? You walk away with this deep, quiet joy. It’s purpose. And it’s bigger than words.
We tend to underestimate how powerful these little acts of kindness can be.
The book shares a story that really brings this to life. Someone starts volunteering at a local shelter, hoping to help out. They expect to make a difference for others—but what really surprises them is how much they get in return. Suddenly, they feel like they belong. Their faith in people gets a boost. They’re reminded, in such a real way, that goodness is all around us.
Here’s something to pay attention to:
Service isn’t about grand gestures or sacrificing everything you have. It’s about showing up, heart open, again and again. Sometimes it’s just listening. Or being fully present. Or meeting someone right where they are, without judgment.
Maybe you’ve thought, “I don’t have anything to give,” or “What difference can I really make?” But the truth is, every act of love—no matter how small—has a ripple effect. Most of the time, we’ll never even see where those ripples go.
The invitation here is simple: look for those everyday moments to serve. Offer a smile. Share a kind word. Lend an ear. Over time, these small gestures weave themselves into your days. Love in action becomes part of who you are.
And as you keep going, something beautiful happens. You realize service isn’t a chore—it’s a privilege. It’s how we join in the flow of something bigger than ourselves. The more you give, the more you find yourself filled up.
In caring for others, you discover your own wholeness.
